questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial that the destination would be somewhere related to my major and therefore be benefitting in my studies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything was quite the process and most things were in Japanese. There were so much paperwork.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Some of the students in my dorm went with me to the ward office to fill out some paperwork, that was helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I just lived in one of the dorms provided by the university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Get insurance incase you get hurt or harm someone else on the way to and from school.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very stressful, there were a lot of paperwork. It was also a bit expensive.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was one advisor, but again, the registration was in the holidays so the reply time was very slow.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was quite a hassle, at first I didn´t get into half of the courses I registered for and did therefore not have enough credits. Then I was allowed to apply for more courses as an exception, but when I finally had enough credits, one of my courses got cancelled because of lack of participants. Luckily they made another exception for me to apply for other courses. In the end they found out they had miscalculated the IJL course line, so instead of 9 credits, it was 8 credits. Then everyone in my class was allowed to apply for additional courses if needed.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The documents written and signed by the professors can be send after the deadline, as it is out of your control that the registration period is in their vacations.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The Japanese courses were around the N2 level. My lecture for humanity courses were each 2 credits but had the same workload as the 15 credit courses at KU, the only difference is that their expectations for you are lower.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I quite liked that you were evaluated the whole way through the semester, and not just with a final exam at the end of the semester. Therefore if you do bad on your final exam, it wont be a whole semester wasted. It was also motivating to do well the whole semester through.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 3 lecture for humanity courses, 1 special lecture course, Japanese listening and speaking, Japanese comprehensive, Japanese writing.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: 11616:Lecture for Humanities (LR) - We learned about the art of translation. I was very interesting, but it was favorite course because it was the course I felt the most comfortable in. Each class we would sit in a circle and discuss the translation of different work. One could speak freely, so it was a very pleasant experience. I don´t think I´ve ever spoken that much in any other class before. It did have some of the bigger presentations and exams, but even doing them and discussing them afterwards in the class was a good learning experience.

questions.answer: There´s a surprising amount of insurances you have to pay each month

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most books are cheaper here than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of options, but I had class from 10:40-17:50 most days with daily homework that would take around 2-5 hours to do, so I did not have enough time to enjoy the clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was almost every kind of sport, art and even a club where you could go around and feed the school cats

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I went to the art club once, there was a very relaxing atmosphere.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit the shrines and temples in Kyoto. Kinkaku-ji is located very close to the school.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took about a week to adjust, so I think it was quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Eat together in the canteen, go to a café close by the school, get a language partner, study in the BBP (a lot of Japanese students go there to study English), join a club, register for courses with both local students and exchange students, live in one of the dorms.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Most people don´t speak English here. It is still mandatory to wear masks here. Everything is done through paperwork here, you cannot do things fully online, like in Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food is so good. Everyone is polite. I do not have to worry about randomly getting yelled at by a stranger or hostility from security guards and police.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get used to studying and doing your homework every single day, the dorm kitchen is the best place for you to make friends, speak up in class - it´s the best way to learn something.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring everything you need from home so you don´t have to spend all your money buying basic necessities here. There´s school everyday, even on national holidays, and if school or class is cancelled, you will have a makeup class in the weekends instead.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My Japanese has improved a lot.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Most of my classes were completely in Japanese, so it was hard to follow along the first month or two.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
